clue.text: Ran down tail?

definitions.meaning: to run someone down behind their back, disparage them, is the past tense of backbite
a tail is the rear part of an animal, read whimsically as its hindmost portion

explanation.surface: A terse question: did something run down a tail?
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word into BACK BIT, a jokey description of a tail; the question mark flags that whimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Backbite means to slander someone absent; its past tense matches 'ran down' in the sense of criticised.

clue.text: Types to buzz around firm, primarily managers or "suits"

indicators.note: the buzzing creatures go around the firm and the manager's initial

parts.note: bees are creatures that buzz
CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of the word managers

explanation.surface: Busy types buzz round a company's managers, the 'suits' of the business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suits' looks like the office staff it describes in the surface, but it is a verb: a hat that suits you flatters you.
explanation.definitionFit: A colour that suits you flatters you, and 'becomes you' carries the same sense.

clue.text: Paper produced after rags have been collected

definitions.text: Paper produced after rags have been collected

parts.words: Paper produced after rags have been collected
parts.note: rags are jokingly coats left with an attendant, and a slip is handed over when they are taken in

explanation.surface: Paper manufactured from rags gathered up for recycling.
explanation.walkthrough: Rag paper is a real product, so the surface reads as papermaking; 'rags' are coats handed in at a venue.
explanation.definitionFit: The slip is the numbered stub you receive when your coat is checked in.

clue.text: Book from past — I love plot concealed

indicators.note: the I, love and plot letters are concealed within the past word

parts.note: by means past, as in 'walk by'
O is love, zero in tennis
to plot data is to graph it

explanation.surface: A book about the past in which a love plot lies hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' gives O by the tennis convention of love meaning zero, and 'past' is the preposition, as in walking by.
explanation.definitionFit: A life story written as a volume is a type of book.

clue.text: Farm animal in street overturned vehicles

indicators.note: the animal is placed in the turned street
in a down clue overturned turns the street letters upside down, reading them backwards

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A farm animal wanders into the street and overturns vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' reads the street abbreviation upward in this down entry, giving TS.
explanation.definitionFit: Trams are street-running passenger vehicles on rails.

clue.text: Pet in northeast town? Fashion to be avoided

indicators.note: something to be avoided is kept out, so the fashion word is dropped from the town

parts.note: Darlington is a town in County Durham, north-east England
ton is an old word for high fashion, as in 'the ton'

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a pet in a northern town shuns fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be avoided' removes TON from DARLINGTON, a market town in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A darling is a favourite, a pet, as in teacher's pet.

clue.text: Male odd in female attire — is that not conjuring up a picture?

indicators.note: the jumbled male letters go in the dress

parts.note: a dress is a woman's garment

indicators.note: odd signals the male letters set in a strange order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man oddly dressed in women's clothing: surely an unimaginable sight?
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges the four letters of Male into EAML; 'is that' only links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamless sleep has no dreams, so no images are summoned in the mind.

clue.text: Modern miss with jumper on shares accommodation

indicators.note: in a down entry the jumper sits on top of the title

parts.note: a roo, kangaroo, is a jumper
Ms is the modern title for a woman

explanation.surface: A modern young woman in a jumper shares a flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' suggests a sweater but is the kangaroo; 'on' puts ROO above MS.
explanation.definitionFit: To room with someone is to lodge together, sharing living quarters.

clue.text: Player, inert, transformed with stimulants

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so the two words are rearranged together

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sluggish player is perked up by stimulants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed' rearranges INERT plus STIMULANTS; 'with' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A musician who plays an instrument is a player.

clue.text: Girl mixing with men is a mischievous sort

indicators.note: mixing stirs the letters of the girl and the men together

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl who mixes with men is labelled a troublemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixing with' rearranges GIRL and MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A gremlin is an imaginary imp blamed for faults, a mischievous creature.

clue.text: He's a cool customer, almost ridiculously sweet

indicators.note: arranged ridiculously, so the gathered letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: the contraction is taken letter by letter, the apostrophe ignored
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so the last letter of customer is lost

parts.note: taken as written before losing its final letter

explanation.surface: A calm, unflappable man is described as almost absurdly sweet-natured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims customer to CUSTOME; 'ridiculously' shuffles HES A COOL CUSTOME into the dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A chocolate mousse is a light whipped pudding, a sweet in British usage for dessert.

clue.text: Producer starts with most actors keen entering rehearsals

indicators.note: the starts of the following five words are taken, one letter from each

explanation.surface: A producer is keen to have most of the cast present when rehearsals begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' takes the opening letters of most, actors, keen, entering, rehearsals.
explanation.definitionFit: A maker is one who produces or manufactures something, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Every six months or less, a term that's flexible

indicators.note: letters described as flexible can bend into another order, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An academic term described as roughly half-yearly, give or take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's flexible' rearranges LESS A TERM; 'or' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Semestral describes something happening each half-year, from Latin for six-monthly.

clue.text: Prize exhibit women kept in store that is next to church

indicators.note: the women's letter is held within the store word

parts.note: a store is a shop
W is the abbreviation for women, as on toilet doors
i.e., abbreviated IE, stands for 'that is'
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A prized display item sits in a shop, beside a church, minded by women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept in' sets the women abbreviation inside the store; IE is the Latin id est, 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A showpiece is an item displayed as a prime example, a prize exhibit.

clue.text: Material obtainable from ores — metal

indicators.note: the answer is obtained by reworking the letters of ores and metal

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A material that can be extracted from ores: metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obtainable from' rearranges ORES METAL; the dash is just punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: An elastomer is a rubbery polymer, a kind of material.

clue.text: Term for old German covers master race's member

indicators.note: the German term covers, wraps round, the master's letters

parts.note: Hun was a derogatory wartime term for a German
MA is a Master of Arts

explanation.surface: A grim note on old prejudice: the Germans and the notion of a master race.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the Nazi 'master race'; the definition is a member of the human race.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the human race is a person, a fellow being of our species.

clue.text: Rather shattered at end of exercise — with this going up?

indicators.note: shattered breaks the word rather into pieces to reassemble

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of exercise

explanation.surface: Someone rather shattered after exercise, their pulse climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shattered' rearranges RATHER into HEARTR; then AT and E (end of exercise). 'shattered' also means exhausted in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulse speed rises during exercise, so this is what climbs as you work out.

clue.text: Embarrassed about sexes sitting next to each other, ensconced on sofa?

indicators.note: the bashful word goes about, around, the pair of sexes

parts.note: coy means shy or bashful, as an embarrassed person may be

parts.words: sexes sitting next to each other
parts.note: M and F, male and female, placed side by side

explanation.surface: A shy pair, man and woman, sit awkwardly side by side on a sofa.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example of the state rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone snugly ensconced on a sofa is cosy and relaxed, an example of feeling at ease.

clue.text: A cut is nasty, cut initially stinging

indicators.note: a nasty version of the words is a distorted one, so A CUT IS is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the second cut

explanation.surface: A nasty cut stings at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' rearranges A CUT IS into CAUSTI; 'initially' adds C from the second 'cut'.
explanation.definitionFit: Caustic remarks are biting and sharp, figuratively stinging.

clue.text: Sailor getting damaged kept dry

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
something stained is spoilt or marked, so damaged

explanation.surface: A sailor whose clothes got damaged managed to keep them dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept dry' means stayed off alcohol, not kept out of water: a sailor's surface trap.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to refrain from drink, so a teetotal stretch is staying dry.

clue.text: Action in which bear making great effort is drowned

indicators.note: the carrying word sits in which, inside, the action word

parts.note: a deed is an act or action
to lug is to carry, bear, something heavy with effort

explanation.surface: A dramatic scene in which a struggling bear drowns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bear' is a verb, to carry, not the animal the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Deluged means flooded or swamped, overwhelmed by water.

clue.text: Like burglars one's seen outside home very briefly

indicators.note: the united word is seen on the outside of the home letters and V

parts.note: people who are as one are united
in means at home
V is the short form of very

explanation.surface: Someone spotted outside a house very briefly, like a prowling burglar.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', a link; 'one' means together as one.
explanation.definitionFit: Burglars arrive without any invitation, so they are guests nobody asked.

clue.text: Screen guest with the thing being hidden

indicators.note: the thing's letters are hidden away, removed from the guest word

parts.note: a visitor is a guest
it means the thing

explanation.surface: A guest screens off the thing to keep it hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being hidden' removes IT from VISITOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A visor is a shield over the eyes or face, a protective screen.

clue.text: Left-side entry made by old-fashioned socialite with sex appeal

parts.note: a deb, debutante, was a young woman entering society
it is old slang for sex appeal, as in the 'It girl'

explanation.surface: A debutante with allure makes a grand entrance from the left.
explanation.walkthrough: In bookkeeping, debits go on the left of a ledger and credits on the right.
explanation.definitionFit: In double-entry accounts the debit column sits on the left side.

clue.text: Dog competition in which one slips a place

indicators.note: the numeral shifts one position along within the competition word

parts.note: a trial is a contest, as in sheepdog trials
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: At a dog show, one competitor slips down a place in the rankings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slips a place' moves I one step right in TRIAL. 'Dog' is a verb here: to follow closely.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to follow them persistently, to track or shadow them.

clue.text: Bad boy at school would have had to be hard to prevail against

definitions.text: Bad boy at school would have had to
definitions.meaning: a naughty pupil in the old days had to endure a caning, receiving punishment
said of a formidable rival or record that is tough to better

explanation.surface: A recollection of old school discipline and of a difficult opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is literal: a bad boy had to accept some beating, i.e. corporal punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something so good that besting it would be very difficult.

clue.text: A "grubby" person coming to the party?

definitions.text: A "grubby" person coming to the party?

parts.words: A "grubby" person coming to the party?
parts.note: grubby is read as to do with grub, food, so the person brings the food to an event

explanation.surface: A grimy guest turning up at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grubby' looks like dirty but means providing grub, slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: A food supplier for events provides the grub at functions and parties.

clue.text: Quaint boy sent a message

parts.note: twee means quaint or affectedly cute
Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A quaint little boy sends someone a message.
explanation.definitionFit: On social media, posting a short public post is called tweeting, so the past form means sent a message.
